name: Kente
description: Kente is a colorful woven textile associated with Ghana, particularly the Asante and Ewe peoples. Its geometric patterns and colors are widely recognized in Ghanaian cultural celebrations.

name: Adinkra Cloth
description: Adinkra cloth is traditionally decorated with symbols that communicate ideas, values, and proverbs. It is associated especially with Akan communities in Ghana.

name: Fugu
description: Fugu, also called batakari, is a traditional smock made from narrow woven strips. It is strongly associated with northern Ghana and is worn for cultural occasions and everyday use.

name: Adire
description: Adire is a Yoruba textile tradition known for indigo-dyed cloth. Artisans create patterns using resist-dyeing techniques such as stitching, tying, and applying paste.

name: Aso Oke
description: Aso Oke is a traditional handwoven textile associated with Yoruba communities. It is often used for special garments, weddings, festivals, and other important occasions.

name: Akwete Cloth
description: Akwete cloth is associated with the Igbo community of southeastern Nigeria. Traditionally woven on looms, it features distinctive patterns and is used for clothing and ceremonial purposes.

name: Ankara
description: Ankara is known for its bold colors and repeating prints. Although often associated with African fashion, its wax-print history includes influences from Indonesian batik and European textile production.

name: Bogolanfini
description: Bogolanfini, often called mud cloth, is a Malian textile traditionally decorated with patterns made using fermented mud and plant-based dyes. It is valued for its craftsmanship and cultural associations.

name: Faso Dan Fani
description: Faso Dan Fani is a cotton textile made from woven strips and associated with Burkina Faso. It is an important expression of local weaving traditions and national cultural identity.

name: Kuba Cloth
description: Kuba cloth is produced by communities in the Kuba cultural region. Made from raffia palm fibers, it is known for intricate geometric designs, embroidery, and cut-pile techniques.

name: Barkcloth
description: Ugandan barkcloth is made by processing the inner bark of certain fig trees. It has a long cultural history in the Buganda region and is used in ceremonies and contemporary artistic work.

name: Kanga
description: Kanga is a colorful rectangular cloth commonly worn in East Africa. Many kangas feature a central design, decorative borders, and a Swahili saying or message.

name: Shweshwe
description: Shweshwe is a printed cotton fabric widely associated with South African dressmaking and heritage fashion. It is recognized for its intricate repeating patterns and distinctive color combinations.

name: Basotho Blanket
description: The Basotho blanket is an important textile in Lesotho, worn for warmth and cultural occasions. Different designs and patterns have become recognizable parts of Basotho identity.

name: Korhogo Cloth
description: Korhogo cloth is associated with the Senufo people of northern Côte d'Ivoire. Traditionally made from handwoven cotton, it is decorated with painted motifs inspired by animals, people, and cultural life.
